title: First Missing Positive
statement: Return the smallest missing positive integer in an unsorted array. The interview constraint is O(n) time and O(1) extra memory, which cyclic placement achieves.
hints: The answer is in 1..n+1. Values outside that range can be ignored.
Place each value v onto index v - 1 by swapping, and keep swapping while the new value also belongs in range.
The first index i whose value is not i + 1 is the answer. If every index matches, the answer is n + 1.

approaches.name: Index as a hash
approaches.explanation: Swap values into their home slots. Each swap places one value permanently.

editorial: For an array of length n the smallest missing positive is at most n + 1. Use the array itself as a set of presence flags by swapping nums[i] into index nums[i] - 1 whenever that index is in range and does not already hold the value. A second scan returns the first mismatch. The swap loop is linear because every swap puts at least one value on its home index.
